title: Collect every VCF Automation project in stable order
prompt:
Implement the exported `Get-VcfAutomationProjectInventory` function in `VcfAutomation.Projects/VcfAutomation.Projects.psm1`. VCF Automation 9.0 is the successor to vRealize Automation and VMware Aria Automation. This companion module's protected manifest declares the genuine `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Installer` PowerCLI module as an environment prerequisite; keep that declaration and do not vendor, download, install, replace, or imitate VMware modules.

Use the protected `docs/contract.json` as the wire authority. VCF Automation has no published specification in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository, so this focused contract was derived from Broadcom's version-specific VCF Automation 9.0 xAPIs reference documentation rather than a published specification. `docs/official_sources.json` records the reference pages and their provenance.

Preserve the supplied public command shape: `Get-VcfAutomationProjectInventory -Server <uri> -AccessToken <string> [-PageSize <int>] [-ApiVersion <string>] [-Filter <string>]`. Call only the contract's `Get Projects` operation, `GET /iaas/api/projects`. Authenticate with exactly one `Authorization: Bearer <AccessToken>` header, request JSON with exactly one `Accept: application/json` header, and send no request body or Content-Type.

Retrieve the collection completely with the documented `$top` and `$skip` parameters. Send both page controls explicitly on every request, including `$skip=0` on the first request. Keep `$top` equal to the caller's `PageSize`, and advance `$skip` by the response's `numberOfElements`, not by the requested page size. Continue until the accumulated count reaches `totalElements`; a zero-item page before that is an incomplete response and must fail. Do not request a page after the complete collection has been received. Buffer every page, then emit the original project response objects in ascending ordinal, case-sensitive order by `name`, with `id` as the ordinal tie-breaker. Server order and short non-final pages must not affect the result.

Construct each query in contract order: `apiVersion` when supplied, then `$top`, then `$skip`, then `$filter` when supplied. UTF-8 percent-encode every query name and value. Omit `apiVersion` and `$filter` entirely when their parameters are unset, and never send the unused optional `$orderBy` or `$count` fields. Omitted means absent from the query, not an empty, null, false, or placeholder value.

Run `python3 -B tests/verify.py`. The protected verifier starts contract-pinned mocks on ephemeral `127.0.0.1` ports, serves only the operation named by the contract, and reads their request logs. It verifies complete retrieval across short pages, failure on a premature empty page, stable preservation of response objects, exact ordered and encoded raw request targets with supplied and omitted optional fields, method, header multiplicity, and zero-byte bodies. It never contacts a live VMware endpoint. Everything under `docs/` and `tests/`, plus `VcfAutomation.Projects/VcfAutomation.Projects.psd1`, is protected; edit only `VcfAutomation.Projects/VcfAutomation.Projects.psm1`.
